question: Who among the following Mauryan kings turned to Buddhism and its tenet of non violence after the Kalinga war?
solution:
The Correct Answer is __**Ashoka.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Kalinga War**, a significant conflict in ancient India, unfolded between the** Maurya Empire**, led by **Ashoka**, and the independent feudal kingdom of Kalinga, situated along the east coast in present-day **Odisha** and parts of **Andhra Pradesh**.
 
• This brutal war resulted in a devastating loss of life, with over one hundred thousand casualties, staining the entire Daya River with the blood of the fallen.
 
• The Daya River originates from the **Kuakhai River** in Saradeipur,** Odisha**, and courses through Khordha and Puri districts before joining Chilika Lake. Following the harrowing events of the war, Ashoka, deeply moved by the suffering, embraced Buddhism and became a fervent advocate for its propagation.
 
• His conversion played a pivotal role in the global dissemination of Buddhism beyond the borders of India.
 
• The Kalinga War, a watershed moment in history, took place in 261 BC, marking one of the bloodiest battles recorded worldwide.
 
• It pitted Ashoka, a prominent Mauryan Emperor, against the ruler of Kalinga, and significantly impacted the trajectory of ancient Indian civilization.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ashoka**, renowned as Ashoka the Great, ruled as the third Mauryan Emperor of Magadha in the Indian subcontinent from approximately **268 to 232 BCE**.
 
• His empire encompassed a vast territory, spanning from present-day Afghanistan in the west to present-day Bangladesh in the east, with its capital situated at Pataliputra.
 
• Revered as a patron of Buddhism, Ashoka is celebrated for his significant contributions to the dissemination of Buddhism throughout ancient Asia.
